## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Nakkhattajātaka* (Ja 49) is a short narrative belonging to the Pali *Jātaka* collection [SuttaCentral]. The story's canonical verse opens with the phrase *Nakkhattaṁ patimānentaṁ* ("While awaiting the stars"), framed by a background story set at Jetavana concerning a naked ascetic (*ājīvika*) [Fausböll 1877; SuttaCentral]. In the narrative framework, a rural family arranges a marriage for their son with a young lady from Sāvatthi of equal rank [SuttaCentral]. After fixing the wedding date, the family consults their resident ascetic, who peevishly declares the celestial constellations unfavorable [SuttaCentral; Anandajoti 2010]. Consequently, the party fails to arrive on the appointed day, prompting the bride's parents to marry her to another suitor; when the original bridegroom later appears, he is rebuffed on the principle that a woman cannot be given in marriage twice over [Sarao and Long 2017; Anandajoti 2010]. The tale serves as a moral teaching on seizing one's opportunity without being led astray by superstition or astrological consultations [Anandajoti 2010; SuttaCentral].
